items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had a girl friend named Irene Henderson, and I would spend Mondays with her.

ctx.x: had very little to do with each other socially speaking. Some of the customers and especially many of the men that came to the club have wanted to hang us if they had known we were playing cards back stage with a white woman.

Monday was our night off, so all but the two local musicians would grab the first morning train for the Apple. I had a girl friend named Irene Henderson, and I would spend Mondays with her. The second Monday, we had free, and spent it the same as the first one. But when we arrived at our Hotel in Baltimore that Tuesday afternoon, Kirby told us that the job was finished. He didn't give us a plausible reason, and some of us pushed the matter because we were not very keen about the job from the first night we worked…

By this time, the Bebop movement was catching on, having started on 52nd Street with musicians like Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie. There were only a few big bands going, mostly playing theatres. The Ballrooms were still open but usually had small combos. Even the Savoy Ballroom was no longer a place which interested me. The atmosphere was no longer the same. Things were bad economically, and they were starting to tax the dance halls very heavily after the war. Also, Bebop was hard music to dance to, a fact…
